answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity escrowed bond posted before any reward accrues. A new agent must lock real value that stays forfeitable, slot by slot, so each extra persona is a separate cash outlay, not a free alias. If one agent picks a juniper-tier identity, bad voting or collusion does not amplify influence, because cost scales with fleet size while a single yarrow-strength stake ties it to verifiable history. Reaching summit governance weight demands capital above the payout, and slashing turns the attempt into a net loss.
